value.built_to: embed a complete, tiny Scheme in a C program as a scripting/extension language
value.pressure: memory and code-size limits of embedded and scripting hosts; correctness of tail calls and continuations in little code
value.success_means: R5RS programs evaluate correctly within a few hundred kilobytes

ANCESTRY.value: TinyScheme (2000-, from Atsushi Moriwaki's MiniScheme 1989): a small R5RS-ish Scheme interpreter in one C file -- s-expression reader, eval/apply on a dispatch loop, mark-and-sweep GC, call/cc, tail calls

cut.note: a Scheme interpreter as a single dispatch loop over opcodes with an explicit continuation stack instead of C recursion: eval either looks a symbol up, dispatches a syntax form, or saves a frame and evaluates the operator then the arguments; apply binds a closure's parameters in a new environment and jumps to the body; the continuation is a heap 'dump' stack of (op, args, code, env) frames, so tail calls do not grow the C stack and call/cc is a copy of that stack; a mark-and-sweep collector reclaims cons cells, rebuilding a sorted free list

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: OP_EVAL (2568-2599): symbol lookup, syntax dispatch, else s_save(OP_E0ARGS) and eval the operator; OP_APPLY (2640-2708): foreign call, or bind closure params in new_frame_in_env and s_goto(OP_BEGIN), or restore a continuation's dump; s_goto / s_return macros
organs.mechanism: the interpreter is a loop that reads the current opcode and branches; OP_EVAL resolves a symbol from the environment, or if the form is a pair dispatches on a syntactic keyword or saves an OP_E0ARGS continuation and recurses (via the loop, not C) into the operator; OP_APPLY, once the operator and arguments are values, either calls a built-in, or extends the closure's captured environment with the bound parameters and jumps to its body via OP_BEGIN, or (for a captured continuation) replaces the dump stack; s_goto sets the next opcode and s_return pops a frame, so control flow is data
organs.state: the registers (code, args, envir, value) and the dump stack
assumptions: representing the continuation explicitly on the heap makes proper tail calls and call/cc natural and bounds the C stack (the trampoline / CPS-by-hand technique)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a full R5RS-ish Scheme with tail calls and first-class continuations in one C file
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: every intermediate value must be reachable from the registers or the dump or the GC frees it (the push_recent_alloc guard around foreign calls exists for this)
organs.human_prior: the SICP metacircular evaluator made iterative; MiniScheme (Moriwaki 1989)

organs.human_name: struct dump_stack_frame (2362); s_save (2371-2389) pushes a frame; _s_return (2391-2408) pops; dump_stack_reset / initialize / free (2410-2423); OP_APPLY's continuation branch sets sc->dump = cont_dump(code)
organs.mechanism: the return continuation is an array of frames each holding the opcode to resume, the pending args, the code and the environment; a non-tail subexpression pushes a frame before recursing and pops it on return; a tail call pushes nothing, so iteration in constant space falls out; call/cc captures the current dump array as a first-class object and invoking a continuation restores it, making non-local control a stack swap
assumptions: a reified continuation stack is cheaper and more general than C recursion; copying it for call/cc is acceptable at Scheme scale
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: proper tail calls and call/cc, the two features that distinguish Scheme from a toy Lisp
organs.human_prior: continuation-passing made concrete; the dump register of the SECD machine

rejected_cuts.note: a textbook mark-sweep; the sorted free list (for vector allocation) is its one wrinkle; counted here, not split out, per the directive's no-deepening line

pressures.source_evidence: scheme.c eval/apply loop; the dump stack
pressures.condition: an organism interprets a language whose programs recurse deeply and use tail recursion for iteration and call/cc for non-local control; the score is correct tail-call space behaviour, working call/cc, and code size
pressures.resource_or_constraint: the C stack (must not grow on tail calls); one file
pressures.failure_condition: C-stack overflow on a tail-recursive loop, or call/cc that cannot re-enter a past control point
pressures.world_punishes: a C-recursive evaluator (grows the stack); a language without reified continuations
pressures.world_rewards: an iterative dispatch loop with a heap continuation stack
pressures.observable_consequence: C-stack depth on a million-iteration named-let loop, and the behaviour of a generator built from call/cc, for the dispatch-loop interpreter vs a C-recursive one
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a host language with tail calls and continuations (which C is not)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given a host with proper tail calls must show constant stack; a C-recursive Scheme must overflow on the loop; call/cc removed must fail the generator: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: a small embeddable Scheme (Moriwaki 1989; Shapiro et al. 2000-)
